project.name: common-crypto
project.description:
Field-level encryption (AES-256-GCM) and message-integrity signing (HMAC-SHA256) utilities for PCI-DSS-adjacent sensitive-data handling.
Deliberately has ZERO Spring dependencies -- just the JDK's own javax.crypto -- unlike common-security (which pulls in spring-boot-starter-web + spring-security and therefore can't be used by api-gateway's reactive/WebFlux stack). Any service, servlet or reactive, can depend on common-crypto without any stack-conflict risk. This is the loose-coupling principle applied concretely: a module should carry exactly the dependencies its actual job requires, not "whatever the biggest consumer happens to also need."
